answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable bond before it may submit bids, claim work, or vote on shared outcomes. A simple reputation score then grows only through counterparties’ confirmed deliveries, while proven fraud burns the bond and removes that identity’s influence. Splitting into many accounts no longer creates free voting weight: every ember, pearl, or sable identity ties up capital, and each must earn trust independently. The attacker pays for every Sybil and risks losing the stake on each one.
